entries.title: The frontier paper, refreshed
entries.summary: The paper now covers 5,206 problems, circle at reach 0.759. Solved rows with no resolved year carry part of the signal: without them the 2005 gap holds and the 2021 gap does not. With them, the settled-only gap shows at 2005, 2015 and 2021.
entries.plot_title: Solvability frontier over 5,206 problems: solved inside, open within reach on the ring, open beyond the circle
entries.image_alt: A large circle with solved problems as filled dots in the centre, open problems inside the edge as rings and open problems outside as triangles, coloured by branch.
entries.discussion: 69 solved problems outside mathematics gained dated evidence, so mind holds 10 solved rows and no branch is unsampled. Counting solved only, inside rows settled at 23% against 4.5% at 2005, 17% against 3% at 2015 and 11% against 1% at 2021. Without solved rows that have no resolved year, the 2005 gap holds (p = 0.014) and the 2021 gap does not (p = 0.149). Counting solved or partial, the AUC is near 0.52 throughout. The model postdates every cutoff. Drawing: MIT code output over Apache-2.0 and CC BY-SA 4.0 data, attributed.

entries.title: The solvability frontier
entries.summary: One circle over 5,080 problems. Reach is a problem's highest text similarity to a solved problem; the circle sits at reach 0.781, where nine in ten solved problems sit. 3,846 inside, 1,234 outside.
entries.plot_title: Solvability frontier over 5,080 problems: solved inside, open within reach on the ring, open beyond the circle, labels on the 40 outside problems with the largest pull
entries.image_alt: A large circle with 1,621 solved problems as filled dots in the centre, 2,225 open problems as rings inside the edge and 1,234 open problems as triangles outside, with problem names in two label columns and a legend of eight branches.
entries.discussion: Mathematics holds 4,112 rows and 3,644 of the inside, so the threshold is a mathematics threshold. A backtest at cutoffs 2005 and 2021 reads two ways. Counting solved only, inside rows settled at 21% against 6% and 12% against 1%. Counting solved or partial, 46% against 61% and 43% against 39%. The verdict is inconclusive. Embeddings and neighbours come from the 2026 corpus, so later statements shape the geometry each cutoff is scored on. Drawing: MIT code output over Apache-2.0 and CC BY-SA 4.0 data, attributed.

entries.title: The 5,080-problem set
entries.summary: 71 curated atlas problems and 5,009 ingested rows from formal-conjectures, Wikipedia unsolved lists, Hilbert, Smale, Science 2005 and 2021, DARPA, XPRIZE, Holy Grails, systems neuroscience and solved timelines. 1,621 solved, 903 partial, 2,556 open.
entries.plot_title: Make-up of the 5,080 problems: branch, status, form, source, licence, posed decade, resolved kind and prediction class
entries.image_alt: A grid of stacked bar charts, one per label, each bar split by category with counts, mathematics the longest bar in every branch chart.
entries.discussion: Mathematics holds 4,112 rows; every other branch sits under 260, and mind has 5 solved of 108, so the set reads the sciences against a mathematics frontier. Licences: 3,557 rows Apache-2.0 from formal-conjectures, 1,154 CC BY-SA 4.0 from Wikipedia, DARPA and XPRIZE, 71 MIT, and 288 cited as headlines under 15 words with paraphrased statements from the Science, ACS and Library of Congress lists. 325 dated rows carry posed years for the backtest. Chart: MIT code output over Apache-2.0 and CC BY-SA 4.0 data, attributed.

entries.title: Principal components of the problems
entries.summary: Five principal components of the 71 atlas problems from an SVD of centred bge-small embeddings, each named by the eight terms at its two ends.
entries.plot_title: The 71 atlas problems on their first two principal components, labelled, with the terms that load each end
entries.image_alt: Scatter of 71 labelled problems on two axes, number theory at one end of the first axis and photobiology, turbulence and dark energy at the other.
entries.discussion: Component 1 carries 12.6% of the variance and runs from additive number theory and diophantine sets to photobiology, turbulence and dark energy. Component 2, 8.5%, sets Kähler manifolds, string theory and gauge theory against computation, learning theory and AI. Component 3, 5.6%, sets qualia and black holes against redox, electron transport and membrane voltage. Component 4, 4.8%, runs longevity against correlated electrons and lattice QCD. On the full set component 1 split Lean theorems from problems, so the problems-only set is drawn. Drawing: MIT code output over MIT, CC BY-SA 4.0 and Apache-2.0 data, attributed.

entries.title: Problem records and OpenAlex activity
entries.summary: Each of the 71 atlas problems has a record: a Wikipedia statement, key works, yearly activity and arXiv totals from OpenAlex, and repo mentions. Empty records fell from 22 to 0; 54 full, 3 partial, 14 weak; 925 key works; activity for 67 of 71.
entries.plot_title: OpenAlex works per sourced problem, 388 of 499 queried rows with any work; seven of eight branches under 30 rows
entries.image_alt: One stacked bar for mathematics, 499 rows split by works matching the query: 111 with none, 115 with 1 to 9, 153 with 10 to 99, 79 with 100 to 999, 41 with 1,000 or more.
entries.discussion: The records feed the embedding text, so a problem is placed by its statement and its literature. OpenAlex activity also covers 499 of the 5,009 sourced rows, all of them mathematics so far; the free budget is 1,000 requests a day and the run resumes daily. The chart compares no branches for that reason. Chart: MIT code output over OpenAlex CC0 counts for Apache-2.0 and CC BY-SA 4.0 problem rows, attributed.

entries.title: Language questions on the quiz
entries.summary: Four question forms from the Polingual word set, meaning, sound, language and pair, across 27 languages, drawn from 844 word cells and 5,190 pairs. Each person picks languages on /research-os/quiz and in the desktop Work quiz; an empty pick leaves the quiz as it was. Every language question credits Wiktionary under CC BY-SA. These are pieces, short of a course. PRs #575, #577 and #580; #593 trims every choice question to three choices.

entries.title: The desktop app uses less of your machine
entries.summary: Explore scenes draw on demand, spin at 20 fps, rest after 15 s idle and stop when hidden; idle CPU fell from about four cores to under 13% of one. Python jobs run with 4 threads, an 8 GiB address-space cap and nice 10. SQLite gains a checkpoint and a journal limit, so the write log after a 20 MB write fell from 21 MB to under 4 MB. A fresh window profile fell from 127 MB to 8 MB. Open: the protein view still grows about 16 MB per visit.

entries.title: Bucket runs on your computer
entries.summary: The website now exists to download the app. Canon search with the globe, drawer and circle runs offline on a local pack of 364 of 599 excerpts after the rights pass. Path shows a grip sphere and a graph of topics. Every screen uses plain words, with no file dialogs on the default screens.
entries.plot_title: Canon clusters of the Bucket graph, the map behind the canon search globe
entries.image_alt: Scatter of every public node on components 2 and 3 with kernel density contours, colored by canon.
entries.discussion: Quiz stems stay under 15 tokens and options under 5, in six forms: recall, cloze, true or false, estimate, compare, order. A terminal CLI and TUI ship with bkt search, bkt canon show, bkt learn, bkt daily, bkt notes and bkt doctor. The target engine is Rust, with Lean proofs for ranking, grading, scheduling and the payment split. The data standard bucket.data/1 is in draft. What's New takes machine posts as drafts. One private corpus stays out of the pack until its author rules.

entries.title: Solver gap engine
entries.summary: 3,599 problems from DeepMind formal-conjectures mapped as proved or open. The 1,364 open ones with a docstring are ranked by embedding similarity to the nearest solved problem in another file; 31 score 0.8 or above and 5 score 0.9 or above. A Lean test file proves three classical results and sample-tests four claims, Goldbach to 3,000 included.
entries.plot_title: Open problems by similarity to the nearest solved problem in another file, all-MiniLM-L6-v2 over docstrings
entries.image_alt: Histogram of 1,364 open problems by cosine similarity to the nearest solved problem in another file, peaking near 0.58, with 31 at 0.8 or above, 5 at 0.9 or above.
entries.discussion: Matches inside the same file are excluded, since those are variants of one problem; 455 open problems had their closest match there. The top cross-file pairs join related conjectures, such as Kotzig's conjecture with Ringel's, and neighbouring Erdos problems. Similarity measures wording, so a high score marks a problem worth handing to a prover and says nothing about difficulty. Next: run DeepSeek-Prover V2 on the top 50 once a GPU host is set, and fund labs to replicate the empirical checks.

entries.title: Prime directions of the 80k corpus
entries.summary: Twelve orthogonal SVD components of the 80,000 Hours and effective altruism corpus, drawn as one polygon per document.
entries.plot_title: Prime directions of the 80k/EA corpus: 12 orthogonal SVD components of a 5,988 x 13,872 binary document-term matrix
entries.image_alt: Radar chart with 12 spokes, one per SVD component, and one colored polygon per sample document from the 80k corpus.
entries.discussion: Randomized truncated SVD ran on a binary matrix of 5,988 documents and 13,872 terms. The twelve components hold orthogonal to within 1e-6. Component 1, developed, leading and models, carries 2.1% of the variance. Component 2, reviewed, monitoring, randomized and mortality, carries 1.7%. Operations, skills and hiring follow at 0.85%, then technology, safety and China at 0.53%. Each polygon is one document's standardized scores. A gap analysis against other public corpora ranks charity, pledges, neglected causes and careers highest for 80k.

entries.title: Canon clusters of the Bucket graph
entries.summary: Twelve SVD directions over the public Bucket graph sort 1,669 nodes into 20 canons.
entries.plot_title: Canon clusters of the Bucket graph: 12 SVD directions over 1,669 public nodes, 20 clusters numbered by PageRank mass
entries.image_alt: Radar chart with 12 spokes, one per SVD direction of the Bucket graph, and one colored polygon per sample node.

extra_images.alt: Scatter of every public node on components 2 and 3 with kernel density contours, colored by canon.

entries.discussion: Each node's features are its terms plus its link columns, idf-weighted and row-normalized. A node joins the pole of its strongest direction. Modularity comes to 0.286, against -0.002 for shuffled labels, 0.773 for the editorial branches and 0.860 for Louvain. NMI against the branches is 0.35. Four of the canons: Canon 2 on mitochondria, melanin and topology, Canon 3 on light and the universe, Canon 4 on computer science and theory, and Canon 8 on water and the exclusion zone.
